---
title: "Step 8: Source Remediation"
---

See **_Appendix 8.1 Source Zone Remediation_** for more info.

## Percent Source Mass Removed by Remediation

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">

| **Parameter** | **Percent Source Mass Removed By Remediation** |
|---|---|
| **Units** | Percent. |
| **Description** | Percent of source mass removed by source remediation activities.<br><br>PFAS source remediation is quite different compared to chlorinated solvent source remediation for the following reasons: 1) PFAS are not DNAPLs; 2) considerable PFAS mass likely exists in the shallow unsaturated zone; and 3) no proven in-situ remediation technologies have yet been developed that can destroy PFAAs. Therefore, for PFAS source removal/isolation, the key remediation technologies at this time are:<br>*Excavation of PFAS-impacted soils.*<br>The simplest method for modeling source remediation assumes that excavation removes nearly all (100%) of the PFAS being modeled.<br><br>&bull; If detailed estimates of PFAS mass are available for both the planned excavated soil volume and the remaining unexcavated soil, these estimates can be used to calculate a percentage of mass removal for REMFluor-MD from an excavation project.<br>&bull; It is important to note that, in general, long-chain PFAAs, particularly PFOS, are more likely to be retained in the upper few feet of the unsaturated zone, whereas short-chain PFAAs like PFBS tend to be distributed throughout the entire unsaturated zone.<br>&bull; At some sites complete excavation of the vadose zone soils may be possible. At a much more limited number of sites dewatering can be performed to removed saturated zone soils impacted by PFAS.<br><br>*Capping to reducing PFAS loading through source isolation.*<br>&bull; Capping involves constructing impermeable <covers over PFAS sources in the unsaturated soil zone.<br>&bull; This method can significantly reduce the amount of PFAS entering groundwater by limiting water infiltration, which in turn decreases PFAS leaching.<br>&bull; Note that some PFAS sources may already be present in the saturated zone, either sorbed (attached) to soil particles, or diffused into low-permeability soils, which can later lead to back-diffusion of these PFAS out of the low-permeability soils and into transmissive aquifer zones.<br>This source concentration reduction starts in "Source Treatment Year" and ends at the end of the model simulation (e.g., no on-off source treatments).<br>See *[Appendix 8.1 Source Zone Remediation]* for more information. |
| **Typical Values** | 50% to 100%. |
| **Source Of Data** | Personal knowledge, vendor information, data from the scientific literature, or performance data from multiple site databases. |
| **How To Enter Data** | Enter directly. |

</div>

## Source Treatment Year

<div style="overflow-x: auto;">

| **Parameter** | **Source Treatment Year** |
|---|---|
| **Units** | Year (YYYY) or yrs. |
| **Description** | Time when source remediation starts. Note that the Toolkit assumes that the year of simulation is the year when the source release occurs. |
| **Source Of Data** | Site history or remediation plans. |
| **How To Enter Data** | Enter directly. |

</div>
